title: How Does a Polar Bear Walk on Ice? Polar Bear Feet
description:
How Does a Polar Bear Walk on Ice? Polar Bear Feet A quick animal fact for kids with Milo the bluebird, from the lesson “Amazing Animal Feet! Paws, Claws and Toes for Kids”.
Polar bear: wide, large, paddle-like feet; 5 toes on each foot; claws non-retractable, 5-7 cm long; soles of feet have small dermal bumps (papillae) that may help with traction on ice; even foot pads are furred in winter; covered with fur except for the nose; 5-10 cm of fat, and both fat and pelt provide insulation (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'Polar Bear', Physical Characteristics, ielc.libguides.com/sdzg/factsheets/polarbear/characteristics, read Nov 16 2026).

description:

title: Why Does an Elephant Flap Its Big Ears?
description:
Why Does an Elephant Flap Its Big Ears? A quick animal fact for kids with Milo the bluebird, from the lesson “Hot or Cold? How Animals Stay Cool for Kids”.
African elephant: large ear surface area with networks of vessels close to the skin surface allow heat to leave the body; flapping the ears dissipates a lot of body heat; wrinkles help the skin retain moisture, and water and mud adhere to wrinkly skin, which boosts evaporative cooling; elephants spray dust, grass and water on the body; they walk on tiptoes with large fat pads cushioning the feet; they may detect vibrations through their feet (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'African Elephants', Physical Characteristics, ielc.libguides.com/sdzg/factsheets/african_elephant/characteristics, read Nov 16 2026).

title: Whose Feet Have Two Hooves? Guess With Milo
description:
Whose footprint has two halves? Guess with Milo the bluebird! It is the giraffe: a giraffe has two hooves on each foot, and its feet are as big as a dinner plate. It walks by moving the two legs on one side together, then the two legs on the other side, so its legs do not bump. And a baby giraffe can stand up and walk about an hour after it is born! title: How Many Fur Coats Does a Polar Bear Have?
description:
How many fur coats does a polar bear have? Two! Count them with Milo the bluebird: a soft, thick undercoat close to the skin, and long guard hairs on top. The long hairs work like a raincoat, and on land water rolls right off. Fur covers almost all of its body. A quick animal fact for kids from the lesson “How Do Polar Bears Stay Warm?”.

title: Why Do Polar Bears Have Furry Feet?
description:
